text:
maya: Heads up — I spotted negative invoice adjustments for a handful of EU free-tier accounts after this morning's quota rollover. Example: acct=acct-47 shows a -0.02 USD line item. Anyone seen this before?

zach: yikes. do you have a sample event or metering rows we can look at?

maya: pasted a small snippet from the events table that looks off:

```
-- snippet from metering.events
account_id | route    | tokens | model                | ts         | dedupe_key
acct-47    | /v1/chat | 12     | redwood/open-chat-1  | 1719119000  | X
acct-47    | /v1/chat | -12    | redwood/open-chat-1  | 1719119200  | X
```

We have a negative token row.

li: negative rows usually come from the dedupe/fixup job. If dedupe runs after invoice cut it writes corrective events with negative tokens. Shouldn't be shown as negative dollar lines on a finalized invoice though.

owen: agreed. invoices should either include adjustments as separate credit lines or defer them to the next invoice. Do we know where in the pipeline the adjustments are materialized?

sam: rough flow: billing-agent -> aggregator -> invoice-generator. My hypothesis: dedupe finished after invoice cut and the aggregator expanded the sampled row, so invoice-generator picked it up when it re-ran. Also sampling interplay might amplify deltas.

billing-bot: Alert: dedupe-job finished: job_id=dedupe-20260320-01 rows_modified=742 latency=3m12s

nora: can we repro on a copy? steps would be: 1) run dedupe on a copy of events for that window, 2) run invoice-generator with the same cut_time, 3) compare invoice line diffs.

zach: another twist — free-tier uses sampling (1/1000) for perf. If we sampled a positive event and later dedupe removed the original, the sampling weight expansion can create a negative adjusted row that, after scaling and rounding, shows up as a small negative USD line.

maya: found more in the logs: from `metering-sample.log` -> `sampled_tokens=12000 sampling_weight=1000`, then dedupe wrote `-12000` tokens. After expansion we report 12 tokens to invoice (12000/1000), rounding produced a decimal that turned into -0.02 USD.

owen: so root causes: late dedupe + sampling expansion + per-line rounding rules. Potential fixes:
- a) hold sampled events until dedupe/stability window passes (adds latency)
- b) apply dedupe to raw events before sampling expansion (more intrusive)
- c) treat post-cut adjustments as pending and surface them as separate credits on the next invoice (quick but customer-visible delay)

sam: short-term I like option c) plus adding an invoice-generator guard that ignores adjustment events that arrived after cut_time (treat them as pending). Longer term b) is ideal.

nora: I'll draft a small patch for invoice-generator to mark post-cut adjustments as pending (so they don't turn into negative finalized lines). PR + runbook. ETA: today EOD.

maya: action items: nora PR for invoice-generator behavior change; sam to run repro and provide affected account list; ops to add a console metric for `negative_invoice_line_count` and alert if >0.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: PR #3141 to staging billing-service (nora).

zach: also need a remediation plan for already-affected invoices — create one-off credit adjustments and notify customers.

maya: agreed. nora, please include a remediation script in the PR and tag @support so they can prepare customer comms.

nora: will do. I'll also add a short postmortem template and link to the repro artifacts.

sam: I'll post the affected account list here once I finish the query.

maya: thanks everyone — I'll own the postmortem and follow ups.
